fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (PC units x Intel revenue per unit; supply-bound DCAI on the CFO's +40% substrate path; segment margins; Foundry/corporate loss) gives FY2027 revenue ~$69.8B / EPS ~$1.41 and FY2028 ~$78.0B / ~$1.95; NTM EPS at the horizon ~$1.92. methods.inputs: Products 23,500 x 15 = 352.5B; Foundry/other -10,105 x 6 = -60.6B; 14A option 18B; net debt at H 0.5B; NCI 16.6B; / 5,506M shares

QCOM (closest mature client-SoC peer) trades 22.4x NTM P/E and 15.1x trailing EV/EBITDA [27]; Intel Products are losing server share to Arm and AMD [17,19], so 15x EV/EBIT (~17x P/E at 12% tax) sits below the peer median. Losses narrowing (Foundry -3,168 Q2 2025 -> -1,853 Q3 2026 [1,2]; 18A cost -40% [18]); capitalising the loss at 6x assumes it fades over ~6 years.

downside.story: P10: PC units fall a further ~6 pts a year below base (memory shortage and OEM destock run through 2027 [16]), client price/mix gives back the 2026 step (-5 pts), DCAI output 15% lower (the +40% substrate lands late and AMD/Arm take the added demand [17,34]; FY2028 ~36.7B, the round-1 path), segment margins 4-6 pts lower, Foundry losses 12% wider with no 14A anchor, the P/E falls 10 turns toward the 22.1x peer median and SOTP multiples drop 15%.

base.story: Median: PC units fall ~25% y/y in Q4 2026 and ~6% in 2027 before a small 2028 recovery; client revenue per unit gives back part of its 2026 step; DCAI grows ~34% in 2027 and ~20% in 2028 as the +40% substrate lands in H2 2027 (less share to AMD/Arm); DCAI margin ~37-38%; Foundry losses narrow slowly; 40.0x on ~$1.92 NTM EPS.

upside.story: P90: PC units recover faster (Counterpoint flat 2027 [15]; NAND prices falling from 2Q27 [37] ease BOM costs), the +40% substrate is fully captured with shortage pricing into 2028 (DCAI +12%, FY2028 ~48B) [34], margins +3-4 pts, Foundry losses narrow 15%, a named 14A customer lifts the P/E 8 turns and SOTP multiples 10%.

reasoning: Industry lane. Round 2 keeps the round-1 PC-side build (Gartner/IDC/Omdia/Counterpoint units [6,13,14,15], TrendForce OEM inventories [16], Intel revenue per unit fading after the 2026 price step) and fixes what the supervisor found: (1) shares: 5,440M CFO Q4 guide [33] + 66M escrow by the horizon, 0% a year, SBC costed once; (2) DCAI built from the capacity path: CFO +40% substrate mostly H2 2027 and industry supply-constrained into 2028 [32,34], less share to AMD/Arm [17,19] -> FY2027 36.0B, FY2028 43.2B (round 1 34.5/37.6B; supervisor booked 37.2/47.9B; its card 41.0B), DCAI margin ~37% in 2028 (round 1 ~35%; booked ~39%) because the shortage runs into 2028; I keep a fade below the booked 39% since Arm/AMD add supply. (3) 14A option (30% x $60B) moved into the SOTP only, since the P/E exit keeps 80% of a premium that already prices foundry optionality; an 18A-P customer signed in November [35,36] supports keeping 30%. (4) Peers re-priced at 11-23 closes on current Zacks EPS: median 22.1x, own 46.4x, exit 40.0x. (5) NCI per CFO ~$1.1B a year. Versus consensus: FY2027 revenue ~69.8B vs Zacks 68.05B (+2.6%), EPS ~1.41 vs 1.31 (+8%, higher DCAI); FY2028 EPS ~1.95 vs one Zacks estimate 3.23 (-40%, I keep Foundry losses ~$10B). Base $68.52 (+15%), P10 $26.62, P90 $120.16 against 86% realized vol. The SOTP Products metric (23,500) is not driver-linked (computed from the build's FY2028 segment EBIT). Q4 2026 8,200 = Q3 7,318 x 1.12, below the CFO's mid-teens sequential (+15% = 8,416 [22]) because ~$300M of the Fab 28 loss is 10nm server [21]. Capacity path (revised round 2): the CFO has secured ~40% more substrate capacity, most of it arriving in H2 2027 [32,34], and expects the industry supply-constrained through 2027 and into 2028 [34]. Q1 2027 8,100 (second ~$300M Fab 28 hit [21]); Q2 8,500 (small early substrate adds, +5%); Q3 9,300 and Q4 10,100 as the H2 substrate lands (+9% a quarter). Q4 2027 10,100 = Q4 2026 8,200 x 1.23: about 60% of the +40% package capacity in place by year-end (the rest in 2028), at constant price/mix. FY2027 36,000 (+34% on FY2026 26,832). FY2028 10,500/10,700/10,900/11,100 = 43,200 (+20%): full year of the +40% substrate (8,200 x 1.40 = 11,480 a quarter at full capture) less ~6% for share ceded to AMD and Arm as their supply also grows (TrendForce Arm ~30% in 2027, AMD rising [17]; AMD server unit share 35.5% Q3 [19]). Demand cross-check: TrendForce server CPU units >+40% 2027 [17]; x86 units ~+40% x 0.70/0.78 = +26% in 2027. Alternatives: round-1 +9% FY2028 (37.6B, -$6 roughly); booked supervisor 47.9B (supply build at +29%).
drivers.why: Disclosed segment kept as a driver because it is capacity-bound: demand (TrendForce [17]) exceeds what Intel can ship, so the informative quantity is Intel's own output.
drivers.variant_view: Substrate arrives late or AMD/Arm take the added demand: FY2028 ~38B (round-1 path), about -$6/share; full capture of +40% with no share loss: FY2028 ~46B, about +$3.

drivers.label: CCPG segment operating margin
drivers.derivation: Actual CCPG operating margin 2025 30.9/26.1/31.6/27.0%, 2026 32.6/26.4/28.2% [1-4]. Q4 2026 22%: revenue down ~20% q/q on a largely fixed cost base (operating deleverage; Q4 company GAAP gross margin guide 37.1% vs 43.0% in Q3 [1]). 2027 23-25% and 2028 25%: volume stays ~10% below 2025, so margin stays below the 2025-26 range (26-33%).
drivers.why: Client margin moves with utilisation of Intel 7/18A client wafers and pricing.

drivers.label: DCAI segment operating margin
drivers.source: Intel releases [1,2,3,4]; Fab 28 [21]; TrendForce [17]; AMD [20]; Futurum [34]
drivers.derivation: Actual DCAI margin 2025 13.9/16.1/23.4/26.4%, 2026 30.5/39.5/41.5% [1-4] on server price increases and full utilisation. Q4 2026 36%: Fab 28 wafer write-offs mostly 10nm server [21]. 2027 37-39%: shortage pricing persists (CFO: supply-constrained through 2027 into 2028 [34]) and volume leverage on the new substrate. 2028 38/37/37/36% (FY ~37%): raised ~2 pts from round 1 because the shortage now runs into 2028 [34], but still below the 41.5% Q3 2026 peak since Arm (~30% of units in 2027 [17]) and AMD [19,20] add supply and Diamond Rapids/Clearwater Forest ramp costs land. Alternatives: supervisor booked ~39% (40% fall-through); round-1 34-36%.
drivers.why: Server pricing and mix are the swing in Intel's profit pool.
drivers.variant_view: Pricing holds at the 2026 peak (41%) once supply loosens: about +$3; price war with AMD/Arm (33%): about -$3.

drivers.label: Foundry + All Other + corporate + eliminations operating income
drivers.derivation: Actual (total operating income - CCPG - DCAI) 2025 -3,237/-5,862/-2,975/-2,879; 2026 -7,194 (incl. Q1 corporate -5,080 restructuring), -3,021, -2,802 [1-4]. Q4 2026 -3,450: Q3 run-rate plus the rest of FY2026 restructuring (~$4.3B FY vs $3,969M nine months [1]) and Fab 28 wafer write-offs [21]. 2027 -2,800 a quarter: Foundry loss improved from -3,168 (Q2 2025) to -1,853 (Q3 2026) [1,2] and 18A cost fell ~40% in 2026 [18], offset by depreciation from a sharply higher 2027 capex [18]. 2028 -2,500 a quarter as 18A matures (14A HVM 2028 adds start-up cost).
drivers.why: Carries the Foundry start-up losses and corporate costs that separate Intel's product profit from group EBIT.
drivers.variant_view: Foundry breakeven path (-1,800 a quarter by 2028): target about +$5; 14A start-up costs without customers (-3,200 a quarter): about -$5.

parts.name: Intel Products (CCPG + DCAI)
parts.note: NTM-at-horizon (~FY2028) CCPG + DCAI segment EBIT from the build (CCPG 7,542 + DCAI 15,978 = 23,520, rounded) x 15x EV/EBIT

parts.name: Foundry, other and corporate
parts.note: NTM-at-horizon loss x 6 (losses capitalised as narrowing over ~6 years of 18A/14A ramp)

parts.name: 14A / external foundry customer option
parts.note: 30% x $60B: value of a named 14A anchor customer before or around the horizon; carried only in the SOTP because the P/E leg's 40.0x already keeps 80% of INTC's premium to peers, which is largely foundry optionality on trough EPS

downside.story: P10: PC units fall a further ~6 pts a year below base (memory shortage and OEM destock run through 2027 [16]), client price/mix gives back the 2026 step (-5 pts), DCAI output 15% lower (the +40% substrate lands late and AMD/Arm take the added demand [17,34]; FY2028 ~36.7B, the round-1 path), segment margins 4-6 pts lower, Foundry losses 12% wider with no 14A anchor, the P/E falls 10 turns toward the 22.1x peer median and SOTP multiples drop 15%.

upside.story: P90: PC units recover faster (Counterpoint flat 2027 [15]; NAND prices falling from 2Q27 [37] ease BOM costs), the +40% substrate is fully captured with shortage pricing into 2028 (DCAI +12%, FY2028 ~48B) [34], margins +3-4 pts, Foundry losses narrow 15%, a named 14A customer lifts the P/E 8 turns and SOTP multiples 10%.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set (Q1 FY2025-Q4 FY2028; 7 actual quarters). Value carried by (1) P/E on the build's own NTM EPS at the horizon (GAAP EBIT, SBC costed, own interest, interest income and NCI lines), weight 0.65, and (2) a two-part sum of the parts (Products EV/EBIT 15x; Foundry/other/corporate loss x 6; 14A option 30% x $60B, carried only here), weight 0.35, because Products and Foundry differ in cycle and risk. No FCF-yield leg: forward levered FCF is negative in FY2026-FY2028 (CFO: negative FCF in 2027 [22]). No DCF (policy). The Products SOTP metric (20,700 = FY2028 CCPG + DCAI EBIT from the build) is not driver-linked (the engine's ntm terms cannot read segment revenue); the Foundry part is linked to other_ebit.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) exit k = 0.8 on a trough-earnings own P/E (46.4x on Zacks); k = 0.6 gives 34.6x, about -8%; (b) the 14A option (30% x $60B), now in the SOTP only (about +$1.6 on the blend); (c) 2028 PC units +3% with no published 2028 forecast; (d) 2024 CCG comparatives used for 2025 rpu actuals not re-opened; (e) DCAI FY2028 43.2B sits between round 1 (37.6B) and the booked 47.9B, from the CFO's +40% substrate path less share to AMD/Arm. Probable financing: another equity raise for 2027 capex ~10% (cash and short-term investments $54.0B [F80,F81] cover the FCF gap); DOC warrants (241M) if Intel owns < 51% of Foundry ~10%: both below 20%, not in the set.
